LESSON: THE ANNUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Life of Jesus Christ
Topic 3.1: The Annunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Annunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: why sexual purity is important, • recite and meditate on Luke 1:37. Why is the birth of Jesus Christ unique?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power
2. retell the Birth of John the Baptist
3. discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE ANNUNCIATION
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Annunciation helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE ANNUNCIATION
Study The Annunciation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power

What this means
In this part you learn to recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Annunciation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Retell the Birth of John the Baptist

What this means
In this part you learn to retell the Birth of John the Baptist. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: retell the Birth of John the Baptist.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Annunciation in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can retell the Birth of John the Baptist. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Annunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Annunciation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Annunciation in your own words. (skill: retell the Birth of John the Baptist)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Annunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power.
3. Practise this skill: retell the Birth of John the Baptist.
4. Practise this skill: discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah.
5. Make one local Kenya example of The Annunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Annunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study The Annunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why sexual purity is important, • recite and meditate on Luke 1:37. Why is the birth of Jesus Christ unique?
2. How is John the Baptist a precursor of Jesus Christ?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Annunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power.
5. Be able to: retell the Birth of John the Baptist.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
